findings.title: the peer sent the leaf certificate alone, with no intermediate
findings.detail: browsers that cached the intermediate will not notice and a fresh client will fail — the most confusing class of TLS bug there is

findings.title: the peer sent 1 certificate(s), 1200 bytes of chain
findings.detail: post-quantum authentication is the next migration and it is a size problem again: an ML-DSA signature is around 3.3 KB where an ECDSA one is 64 bytes, so this chain grows by roughly 4 KB per certificate when it moves. This is the headroom you have today

findings.title: pq-ready — post-quantum key exchange works, including for a client that requires it
findings.detail: nothing to do; re-run after any TLS stack or load balancer change

findings.title: pq-intolerant — post-quantum-capable clients cannot connect at all, while classical clients can
findings.detail: the classical client connected and the post-quantum-capable one was cut off (timeout, reproduced on a second dial): every client that merely *offers* ML-KEM fails here — Chrome and Edge 131+, Firefox 132+, a CDN with post-quantum enabled — while curl and your existing health checks keep passing
